title: Dictation phrases v1
notes: Original synthetic dictation phrases spoken by macOS `say` (voice from bench_options.voice, rate 170) and converted to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV by the dictation-stop bench. Covers very short replies, ordinary sentences, names, numbers/dates/times, emails and URLs, punctuation-heavy text, technical vocabulary, and ~45 s rambling notes. No filler words on purpose: the runner's filler cleanup would remove them and inflate WER. Silence items are pinned 3 dev / 1 holdout and guard against hallucinated text. Changing any text changes the suite fingerprint and the fixture cache key.

Okay so here is where I landed on the kitchen renovation after talking it through with the contractor this morning. The cabinets are going to take about six weeks longer than we planned, which means the countertops slip too, and honestly I would rather wait than rush the install and end up with gaps along the wall. The contractor suggested we use the extra time to redo the lighting, which was always on the maybe list, so I asked for a quote on recessed lights over the island and a dimmer by the back door. I also want to double check that the permit covers the electrical work, because the last thing we need is an inspection surprise right before we move everything back in.

Quick brain dump before I forget everything from the planning session. The big takeaway is that people love the export feature but nobody can find it, so the first job next sprint is moving it out of the settings page and into the main toolbar. Second, the search results feel slow on large workspaces, and I think the fix is caching the recent queries rather than rewriting the whole index. Third, we keep promising a dark mode and we keep pushing it, so either we commit to a date or we stop mentioning it in the roadmap. I lean toward committing, maybe the end of next month, as long as design can hand over the color tokens in the next two weeks.

So for the trip next month, I'm thinking we fly into Porto on the Thursday, spend two nights there, and then take the train down to Lisbon for the weekend. The train is about three hours and it's cheaper than renting a car, plus nobody has to drive after dinner. In Lisbon I'd like one slow day with no plans at all, just walking around and eating, and one day where we actually do the museums and maybe the tram up the hill. We still need to figure out where to stay, and I'd rather have a small apartment with a kitchen than a hotel, because breakfast at home saves a lot of money and time. Let me know if the dates work for everyone.

Notes for the incident review. Around two in the morning the queue workers stopped processing jobs, and the alert didn't fire because the health check only verified that the process was running, not that it was making progress. By the time someone noticed, about four thousand jobs were waiting. The root cause was a lock that never got released after a network timeout, so every worker ended up waiting on the same record. The immediate fix was restarting the workers and clearing the stale lock. The longer term fixes are adding a progress based health check, putting a timeout on the lock itself, and writing a small runbook so whoever is on call at two in the morning doesn't have to guess.

Hey, I wanted to write down a few thoughts after our conversation yesterday, because I don't think I said it very well in the moment. I really do appreciate how much effort you've put into the garden project this year, and I know it has not been easy with everything else going on. My only worry is that we keep adding new beds before the old ones are settled, and then the watering turns into a two hour job every evening. Maybe this season we just focus on the tomatoes, the herbs, and the strawberries, and see how that feels. If we still have energy in August, we can plan the bigger expansion together over the winter.

Summary of the budget meeting. We are about twelve percent over on software licenses, mostly because three teams bought overlapping tools for project tracking. The plan is to pick one tool by the end of the month and cancel the others at renewal, which should save somewhere around forty thousand dollars a year. Travel is under budget, which is nice, but that is mainly because two conferences moved online. Hiring stays the same, two engineers and one designer, and the designer role is the priority. Finance wants an updated forecast by the fifteenth, so please send me your numbers by the tenth, even if they're rough, and flag anything you think might change before the end of the quarter.
